thread:
maria: Heads-up — eu-west3 reporting huge ephemeral NVMe scrub/sweep activity, IOPS saturated, several GPU attach requests are timing out (QA and prod canaries).
ops-bot: alert: local-nvme-iops-spike eu-west3 (severity: high) — 1200 attach failures in last 5m, scrub throughput high.
ashwin: ugh. Is this the nightly janitor overlap?
jordan: looks like it. maria do you have `iostat`/scrub metrics?
maria: pasted a short sample:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         820.0  14500  16384  512000     0      0    35.0    38.2  25.6  1.2    27.0   0.90  98.7
nvme1n1         600.0  9800  10240  345600     0      0    35.4    22.6  19.4  0.9    14.8   0.78  88.2
```
Plus scrub controller logs: `janitor/scrub: starting window 0..45, targets=480, concurrency=12`
lee: that's brutal. concurrency=12 on machines with 50k IOPS baseline will still spike queue depth under heavy write.
natalie: can we throttle the janitor without leaving bad wear backlog? low concurrency but longer window might be safer short-term.
ashwin: quick mitigation plan: 1) scale janitor replicas to 0 in eu-west3 for 3m to let GPU attaches recover, 2) reduce per-node scrub concurrency flag `--concurrency=2`, 3) fallback route new GPU attaches to dedicated-capacity pool while we stabilize.
jordan: step 1 is fastest. downside: increases scrub backlog and possibly increases long-term wear if delayed. cost vs availability tradeoff.
maria: ops-bot shows attach success rate jump from 40% -> 92% after killing one scrub pod earlier today for a smaller incident.
ops-bot: metric update: gpu-attach-queue: 320 -> 18 (3m after mitigation). ephemeral-scrub-queue: backlog +230.
lee: we should prefer rate-limiting the scrub instead of full stop. try `--target-iops=3000` and `--max-concurrent-scrubs=2` then watch.
natalie: I can push a config change to the janitor configmap and rollout a canary to 10% nodes now.
ashwin: also consider a short-term scheduling tweak: mark eu-west3 scratch pool `io-priority=low` for background tasks so GPU attach honors NIC/local scheduler priority.
jordan: longer-term, we need either larger scratch NVMe (more IOPS per node) or split scrub windows by AZ to avoid global spike.
maria: rolling the `--max-concurrent-scrubs=2` change can be done in 60s. doing canary now.
ops-bot: deploy: started rollout `janitor-config-update` -> canary 10% nodes.
maria: canary applied. monitoring iostat + attach queue.
natalie: if canary looks good in 5m, I'll roll to 100% but keep `concurrency=2` for next 2 hours.
lee: please also add a temporary autoscale for dedicated-capacity buffer in eu-west3 (1 extra GPU pool) — ops-sre already approved emergency margin.
natalie: created ticket INTERNAL-4523 to track backlog and follow-up scheduling policy.
maria: initial numbers: attach failures down to 12 in last 2m. iops util dropped ~45%.
ashwin: good. we'll keep this thread updated. leaving note: postmortem if backlog >1000 or if attach failures spike again. :thumbsup:
summary: ephemeral NVMe scrub causing IOPS saturation in eu-west3, short-term throttle/canary and capacity fallback discussed and applied
